facts.text: Cerealia Facula Salt Dome was deployed at Occator Crater (Cerealia Facula) during Dawn at Ceres in 2015.
facts.source: Nature Geoscience (De Sanctis et al. 2020) / Dawn VIR Spectrometer

facts.text: A dazzling 10-kilometer bright dome of sodium carbonate salts and ammonium chloride in the center of Occator Crater. Formed when subsurface brines erupted through cryovolcanic fractures caused by asteroid impact.
facts.source: Nature Geoscience (De Sanctis et al. 2020) / Dawn VIR Spectrometer

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Confirmed the highest concentration of carbonate minerals ever detected outside Earth, proving active hydrothermal or cryovolcanic brine processes in dwarf planets.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Occator Crater (Cerealia Facula).
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration on the Moon.

scenes.kids: Take a look at how I was built. Every part of me had a special purpose.

scenes.kids: Out here, there is no air or weather like on Earth, so I had to work smoothly in the cold.
